items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I lived in a house with the people that he lived in.

ctx.x: I were featured together. And that's when I told him that I was the guy that did that, and he laughed like hell. He said, "I wondered what that foolishness." He said, "Well where did you go?" I said, "Well, I went home and got under the cover, I was so embarassed."

But in Chicago there was a lot of activities, a lot of road bands, you know. Of course, as I said to you before, Dan, theaters and shows were the principal factors. You had Tiny Parham playing in Chicago. Fats was there. You had Earl Hines, Jimmie Noone, Teddy Wilson, Louis Armstrong. Jesse Stone had a band in one of the clubs, and Omer Simeon, you had a lot of the great guys and you had an opportunity to hear a lot of good jazz around. There was a guy named Stumpy Evans. Did you ever hear that name?
